title: Chicken Braised in Milk
subtitle: Italian whole chicken braised in lemon-scented milk with sage
excerpt: A whole chicken braised in milk with garlic, sage, and lemon zest produces extraordinarily tender meat and a curdled, golden sauce that is more interesting than it sounds.
sourceNotes: Pollo al latte is found in various forms across Emilia-Romagna and Tuscany. The milk curdles during cooking to produce caramelised nuggets that are as good as the chicken itself. Popularised internationally by Jamie Oliver.

content.text: The sauce looks curdled and unpromising while it cooks; trust the process and serve it as it is.

items.prepNote: zest only, peeled in strips with a vegetable peeler

content.text: Season the chicken generously inside and out.
Heat the butter and olive oil in the stockpot over a medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken all over for 8 to 10 minutes, turning carefully, until golden on all sides.
Lift out the chicken and tip away any excess fat, leaving just a thin layer.
Put the garlic, sage, rosemary, and lemon zest into the pot. Set the chicken back in on top.
Pour the milk around the chicken. Bring to a gentle simmer on the hob.
Transfer to the oven, uncovered. Roast for 1 hour 20 minutes, basting once halfway through.
Leave to rest for 15 minutes before carving. Spoon the curdled pan sauce over each serving.

items.symptom: Milk has evaporated before the chicken is cooked.
items.cause: Pot too wide or oven runs hot.
items.fix: Top up with 100ml more milk and cover loosely with foil.

items.cause: Milk splashed onto the skin during roasting.
items.fix: Blast under a hot grill for 3 minutes just before resting.

items.symptom: Sauce looks watery rather than caramelised.
items.cause: Oven temperature too low to evaporate the milk properly.
items.fix: Increase heat to 200°C for the final 10 minutes.
